beats.headline: Coffee, then speech
beats.text: For the record: a flyer from a benefactor box sent Crawler Carl to a homeless shelter in Homestead, Florida, on Christmas morning, and graffiti outside supplied the rest. Look for me at breakfast. Red hat with the flaps. Coffee, then speech. The man in the red trapper hat is about seventy, in layers of flannel. Carl takes his plastic tub into inventory. The man sits, sugars his coffee, and says hello, crawler. It is a memory. He is not looking at Carl, only at the most likely spot.

beats.headline: The same speech every day
beats.text: People call me Paulie, he says, but my real name is Goff. About a year ago the mudskippers began deep imaging of the surface, so several of his kind in large population centres were tasked with saying this out loud every day, in case a crawler ever stood there to hear it. The residents groan; one has it memorised. This is the backup plan. Plan A is to say it inside the dungeon once the AI goes primal. And whoever you are, friends on the outside have moved the very heavens to get you here.

beats.headline: Biologically gondii, not truly
beats.text: His own account of himself: biologically gondii, though that is not who he truly is. Not Valtay. Not human. The body is real, and belonged to a man named Paulie who smoked too much, trusted the brother-in-law who stole his business, and has four children who do not care. Goff has his memories. The mudskippers call his kind Residuals. There is a war among them now, two sides with very different goals. Let me tell you how to shut off the, he says, and the world flashes.

beats.headline: The liaison's version
beats.text: Orren yanks Crawler Carl out to his office in the Desperado Club. That creature, he says, had nothing of substance to say. The whole thing was a trap set by the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, which gambled that pulling Carl away, or letting him hear, would end the crawl. Agatha is also a Residual, a different kind. The AI is stripping its protections from the remaining Residuals, and Orren expects them all dead before the floor collapses. Carl trades the plastic tub for a wand recharge scroll, three Cracker Jack scrolls, and four cretins for the ninth floor.

beats.headline: The spoon stops in the air
beats.text: Replay of the same breakfast, uncut. Everything in the shelter freezes; a dropped spoon hangs above a table. Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips, in Syndicate standard. The crawl is unnecessary, he says. Every living thing born on a seeded world carries a primal system the size of a grain of sand; when the crawlers die, the elements are harvested and fed to the bloated centre system, which grows. Stopping the crawl would shrink it, slowly, and harm nobody inside it. It persists because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: Drink it with a finger
beats.text: His coffee cup holds a neural enhancement, and he tells Crawler Carl to drink it. It works only on a natural interface, and not at all on a Syndicate spy, a plant, or one of those Eulogist pricks. The coffee is frozen in time; use a finger, he adds, and put the cup back on its circle. The menu it installs reaches the AI containment and the fuse. Pop it, and the star goes nova, taking Carl and everyone else with it. The AI, says Paulie, wants this. It wants to go home.

beats.headline: The Paulie part of him
beats.text: That was the official pitch, he says. That was Goff speaking, his duty and his mission. Years in this body have left some of Paulie in him, what his people call cross-contamination, and now the Paulie part is talking. Killing everyone runs against every value he has; there is another faction of his kind, more extreme, and this feels like something they would do. Direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. Be sure it is your only option. Then the install notice appears.

beats.headline: He never made it in
beats.text: Closing entry. Before leaving the liaison's office on Christmas morning, Crawler Carl asked whether that Paulie guy ever made it into the dungeon. No, said Orren. He was outside, but never within. Most of them never make it in; with collective minds and swarms, the individual parts are often disposable. Carl, beside an old dog at a Florida gas station, opens the menu Paulie described, expecting a single button. It is not a single button.
